FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Numbers, Counting & Early Math flashcards.

Twenty cards that walk a child from the very first "one" all the way to twenty: a big numeral on top, rows of smiling apples, bananas, cherries and figs to count underneath, and the fruit word to read below. Count what you see, then count what is in the fruit bowl — the numbers stop being a song and start being real.

These cards belong to Class 35 · Numbers, Counting & Early Math on the Kiddo School learning path.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Count the card, then the bowl

    Say the number on the card, then find that many real things: one apple, three oranges, ten blueberries if you are feeling brave. The kitchen is the answer key.

  2. 02

    Lay the cards in order

    Deal the cards out like a number line across the floor, 1 to 20. Walk it, hop it, drive a toy car along it — the order gets into the legs, not just the head.

  3. 03

    Spot the ten-and-more trick

    From eleven onward, every card is ten fruit plus some more. Cover the extra ones and count the hidden ten — that is the whole secret of the teens, learned on paper.

  4. 04

    Race to twenty

    Shuffle the cards, flip one at a time and clap that many times. Get to twenty and the clapper picks tomorrow's snack. Loud, silly and full of counting.

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 1 Flashcard — One Apple for Preschoolers

      One smiling apple under a big black 1 — the card where counting begins, with the word "apple" waiting below to be read too.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Turns the very first number into one proud, holdable apple.

      Make the number real

      Hand over one biscuit and wait for the proud announcement.

      The skill underneath

      That one means a single thing, all by itself.

      Where to stick it

      Fridge door, low down, at grabbing height.

      One more trick

      Point at single things all day — one nose, one belly button.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Numbers, Counting & Early Math (Class 35) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 2 Flashcard — Two Bananas for Preschoolers

      Two smiling bananas leaning together under a big black 2 — the number of pairs, from shoes to socks to the two of you.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Names the pairs your child already wears, eats and counts.

      Make the number real

      Fetch two shoes and count them on, left then right.

      The skill underneath

      Twos are pairs, and pairs are everywhere at home.

      Where to stick it

      Bathroom door, beside the two taps.

      One more trick

      Mismatched sock hunt — only true pairs survive the wash.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 3 Flashcard — Three Oranges for Preschoolers

      Three smiling oranges in a row under a big black 3 — small enough to count at a glance, big enough to feel like real counting.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Keeps counting small enough to finish before the wiggle starts.

      Make the number real

      Set out three snacks and count each into the plate.

      The skill underneath

      Three things can be counted one at a time, in order.

      Where to stick it

      Play kitchen wall, where snack numbers live.

      One more trick

      Stop at three even mid-game; clean endings build trust.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 4 Flashcard — Four Strawberries for Preschoolers

      Four smiling strawberries standing in a row under a big black 4 — the number of table legs, dog paws and chair feet.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Matches a numeral to the fours underfoot — table legs, paws.

      Make the number real

      Crouch under the table and count the four legs aloud.

      The skill underneath

      The same four can look like legs, paws or berries.

      Where to stick it

      Four corners of the play table, one card.

      One more trick

      Count the dog's paws next — four again, different body.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 5 Flashcard — Five Pears for Preschoolers

      Five smiling pears arranged two up and three below under a big black 5 — the number that fills one whole hand.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Fills one whole hand for the first time — five, all there.

      Make the number real

      Press one hand flat on the five after counting each finger.

      The skill underneath

      Fingers are a number line a child never leaves at home.

      Where to stick it

      By the sink, where hand-washing gets counted too.

      One more trick

      Hide a hand behind your back and ask what went missing.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 6 Flashcard — Six Grapes for Preschoolers

      Six smiling grape bunches in two rows of three under a big black 6 — the first number that will not fit on one hand.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Stretches counting past one hand, which is where it gets interesting.

      Make the number real

      Lay six snack grapes in two rows of three, like the card.

      The skill underneath

      Bigger groups still get counted one by one, no rushing.

      Where to stick it

      Snack shelf, guarding the fruit bowl.

      One more trick

      Two rows of three is the dice-six shape — say it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 7 Flashcard — Seven Cherries for Preschoolers

      Seven smiling cherries, four above and three below, under a big black 7 — the number of days in a whole week.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Borrows the week's seven days and gives them cherries.

      Make the number real

      Tap one finger per day and name all seven days out loud.

      The skill underneath

      Numbers keep going after five, in order, without dropping any.

      Where to stick it

      Calendar wall, right beside the week.

      One more trick

      Trace the 7 with a finger; it confuses one and seven.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 8 Flashcard — Eight Watermelons for Preschoolers

      Eight smiling watermelon slices in two rows of four under a big black 8 — the number with two stacked circles, like a snowman.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Shows a number with two stacked circles, like a snowman numeral.

      Make the number real

      Break a snack into eight pieces, lay them out, count, then eat.

      The skill underneath

      Long counts need slow voices and steady pointing fingers.

      Where to stick it

      Picnic basket clip — sliced fruit lives here.

      One more trick

      Count like an octopus, arms out, one clap per slice.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 9 Flashcard — Nine Peaches for Preschoolers

      Nine smiling peaches grouped four, three and two under a big black 9 — standing right next door to ten, the number every counter is aiming for.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Stands one step below ten, close enough to shout about.

      Make the number real

      March nine hallway steps there and nine back again.

      The skill underneath

      Nine has neighbours — eight behind, ten just ahead.

      Where to stick it

      Hallway height, at walking-eye level.

      One more trick

      Countdown from nine turns tidy-up time into blast-off.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 10 Flashcard — Ten Blueberries for Preschoolers

      Ten smiling blueberries in two neat rows of five under a big black 10 — all ten fingers, counted and claimed at last.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Delivers the big one — all ten fingers counted and finally claimed.

      Make the number real

      Clap ten times, counting each one, hands and voice together.

      The skill underneath

      Ten is two hands, two rows of five, one proud number.

      Where to stick it

      Bedroom door, the exit to number land.

      One more trick

      Celebrate reaching ten loudly; finish lines deserve noise.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 11 Flashcard — Eleven Kiwis for Preschoolers

      Eleven smiling cut kiwi halves showing their green centres under a big black 11 — the first number after ten, where counting keeps going.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Opens the teens with ten kiwis and one bold newcomer.

      Make the number real

      Line up ten blocks, add one more and announce eleven together.

      The skill underneath

      After ten, counting keeps going — ten and one more.

      Where to stick it

      Above the ten card, one step up.

      One more trick

      Eleven breaks the -teen pattern; give it a slow say.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 12 Flashcard — Twelve Lemons for Preschoolers

      Twelve smiling lemons in three rows of four under a big black 12 — a dozen, the word bakers and egg-boxes use for exactly this number.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Introduces a dozen, the word bakers and egg boxes use.

      Make the number real

      Point at twelve months on the calendar, one finger each.

      The skill underneath

      Twelve is a dozen — a real grown-up counting word.

      Where to stick it

      Kitchen wall, near the egg box.

      One more trick

      Three rows of four — same twelve, tidier shape.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 13 Flashcard — Thirteen Pineapples for Preschoolers

      Thirteen smiling pineapples with green crowns, grouped five, five and three, under a big black 13 — the teen word everyone trips over, on its own card.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Gives the trippiest teen word its own card and its own say.

      Make the number real

      March thirteen stairs, one word per step, slowly all the way.

      The skill underneath

      Thir-TEEN said slowly stops being a tongue trap.

      Where to stick it

      Stair rail, next to the banister.

      One more trick

      Whisper the teen ending like a secret; it helps.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 14 Flashcard — Fourteen Raspberries for Preschoolers

      Fourteen smiling raspberries, grouped five, five and four, under a big black 14 — ten berries and four more, wearing two week's worth of days.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Splits neatly into ten berries and four, the pattern behind every teen.

      Make the number real

      Count out ten things, add four, then say ten and four makes fourteen.

      The skill underneath

      Every teen is a ten plus some more.

      Where to stick it

      Chore chart corner, where days get tallied.

      One more trick

      A fortnight means fourteen days — two weeks of sleeps.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 15 Flashcard — Fifteen Mangoes for Preschoolers

      Fifteen smiling mangoes in three rows of five under a big black 15 — ten fingers counted, then five toes to finish the job.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Runs out of fingers at ten and finishes on five toes.

      Make the number real

      Wiggle through ten fingers and five toes, landing on fifteen.

      The skill underneath

      Ten fingers plus five toes is fifteen, honestly counted.

      Where to stick it

      Shoe rack, where feet get counted twice daily.

      One more trick

      Rows of five again — three fives live inside fifteen.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 16 Flashcard — Sixteen Coconuts for Preschoolers

      Sixteen smiling brown coconuts, three rows of five plus one, under a big black 16 — ten and six more, sturdy as the nut itself.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Builds a square — sixteen coconuts in four tidy rows of four.

      Make the number real

      Stack sixteen blocks into a four-by-four square and count all sides.

      The skill underneath

      Same number, two shapes — a line and a square.

      Where to stick it

      Toy shelf, holding the blocks nearby.

      One more trick

      Four rows of four is called a square number, someday.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 17 Flashcard — Seventeen Apples for Preschoolers

      Seventeen smiling red apples, grouped six, six and five, under a big black 17 — proof that counting stays steady well past two hands.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Proves counting stays steady long past two hands.

      Make the number real

      Clap-count to seventeen, one clap per number, voice steady.

      The skill underneath

      Long counts wobble near the end; steady beats fast.

      Where to stick it

      Music corner, where clapping counts.

      One more trick

      Restart wobbly counts from ten, not one — clever shortcut.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 18 Flashcard — Eighteen Bananas for Preschoolers

      Eighteen smiling yellow bananas in three rows of six under a big black 18 — ten and eight more, one short of the last teen.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Counts eighteen in three rows of six, tidy as the fruit stall.

      Make the number real

      Sort buttons or coins into two rows of nine, then count all.

      The skill underneath

      Rows make big numbers easier to count and to trust.

      Where to stick it

      Money jar lid, coins welcome.

      One more trick

      Three sixes land on eighteen — let your child spot it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 19 Flashcard — Nineteen Apricots for Preschoolers

      Nineteen smiling orange apricots, grouped seven, seven and five, under a big black 19 — the last teen, waiting right outside twenty's door.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Lingers one door away from twenty, the last teen on the shelf.

      Make the number real

      Count nineteen slowly, pause dramatically, and wait for the shout of twenty.

      The skill underneath

      Nineteen waits right outside twenty's door.

      Where to stick it

      Beside the twenty card, one step short.

      One more trick

      Hold the pause before twenty longer than feels natural.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS, COUNTING & EARLY MATH · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Number 20 Flashcard — Twenty Figs for Preschoolers

      Twenty smiling purple figs in four neat rows of five under a big black 20 — two full tens, the summit of the whole set.

      Teaching tips

      What this number carries

      Reaches the summit — twenty figs, two full tens, set complete.

      Make the number real

      Cover one row of five and count what is left, then rebuild.

      The skill underneath

      Twenty can be taken apart into tens and rebuilt.

      Where to stick it

      Hang it highest — A3 if the printer allows.

      One more trick

      Pin all twenty cards across a wall and walk the number line.

      Teach it, step by step
